samples.summary: Adding `readOnlyMount` to the slides mount-effect deps makes the effect body re-run at the moment of an editor→viewer downgrade, and that body performs an ungated `doc.update()` (`ensureSlidesRoot`) — so the downgrade itself triggers a CRDT write from the session that just lost write authority.
samples.evidence: The diff adds `readOnlyMount` to the deps at slides-view.tsx:1237, so on a `/shared/:token` role drop the whole effect body re-executes with `readOnlyMount === true`. Line 282 calls `ensureSlidesRoot(doc, …)` before any read-only check, and `yorkie-slides-store.ts:246` opens a `doc.update(...)` unconditionally (not only when `root.meta == null`), backfilling `themes` / `masters` / `guides` / `meta.themeId` / per-slide `notes`. The in-file comment at slides-view.tsx:276-281 already concedes this is a viewer-write gap ("`ensureSlidesRoot` may run a `doc.update()` migration block when a viewer mounts"); the diff newly makes the *revocation event* one of its triggers. Attacker path: hold an editor share link, keep the tab open, have the owner downgrade the link to `viewer`; the downgrade's own remount writes to the shared deck as the downgraded principal. The two sibling views the diff touches gate their equivalent seeds (`docs-view.tsx:354` `if (!readOnly && !ensureTree(doc)) return;`, `notes-view.tsx:133` `if (!readOnly) ensureText(doc)`), and slides' own deck seed is gated at slides-view.tsx:696 — only `ensureSlidesRoot` is not.

samples.summary: The whole revocation/downgrade story this change builds rests on client-side gates, because the only server-side per-document write check ships in shadow mode by default — a computed deny is logged and then allowed.
samples.evidence: `handleAuth` at yorkie-auth.controller.ts:111 returns ALLOW whenever `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE !== 'true'`, i.e. a deny decision (`hasAccess` → `needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`, line 217) is discarded in the default configuration. The diff's own comments acknowledge this (shared-document.tsx:1099-1103, read-only.ts:38-42: "with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary rather than a convenience in front of one"). Consequence: in a default deployment the *only* thing stopping a revoked or downgraded share visitor from writing to the shared CRDT is the client code this PR edits — a `readOnly` flag, a name allowlist and a Proxy, all of which a visitor holding the page can trivially reach around (e.g. `__docsEditor` is even exposed in DEV, docs-view.tsx:404). Pre-existing and deployment-gated, but the diff increases reliance on it, so it is worth stating: revocation is advisory until enforcement is switched on.

samples.summary: `revocableDocStore` forwards non-function members raw while live and binds mutators to the raw store, so a handle captured before `dispose()` can retain unrevocable write authority — exactly the escape `readOnlyDocStore` deliberately closes.
samples.evidence: In the live state the `get` trap does `if (typeof raw !== 'function') return raw;` (read-only.ts:199), and `getPrototypeOf` forwards the real prototype (read-only.ts:214). `YorkieDocStore.doc` is a data field holding the Yorkie `Document`, whose `update()` is the documented write path — so `editor.getStore().doc` obtained before disposal keeps full CRDT write access after `disposed = true`, and no later check can reach it. `readOnlyDocStore` hides data properties for precisely this reason (read-only.ts:89-96: "Forwarding those would have left a wider hole than the prototype one below"). Same shape for a captured bound mutator: line 202 binds to `target` (the raw store), so `const f = handle.insertText` taken pre-disposal still writes afterwards. I could not find an in-repo holder that captures `.doc` or an individual bound member (docs-find-bar.tsx:66-67 captures the `Doc` and a `() => editor.getStore().snapshot()` closure; docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:496 re-reads `getStore()` per call), which is why confidence is low — but the gate's stated contract is "the handle itself goes dead", and for these two routes it does not.

samples.summary: Client-side link revocation fails open by design: any non-verdict failure keeps the last-good role, so suppressing the revalidation request (offline, blocked host, DNS, devtools request-blocking, backend restart) preserves `editor` authority in the client indefinitely.
samples.evidence: `isRevokedShareLinkError` returns false for a `TypeError` from `fetch()` and for 408/429/5xx, and shared-document.tsx:1138 only treats an error as `fatal` when it is a verdict, so `resolved` (and therefore `readOnly`, shared-document.tsx:335/388/438/465) keeps its previous value. A visitor who wants to keep the editor UI simply has to make one XHR per minute fail — trivially self-inflicted from the browser. There is also an inherent ≤`SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS` (60 s) window after a real revocation. This is an accepted availability trade-off for a client affordance and is documented in the diff; it only becomes a real authorization gap in combination with the webhook's default shadow mode (separate finding).

samples.summary: `insertImageFromFile` performs the upload before consulting `isDisposed()`, so a session whose authority was revoked mid-flight still pushes bytes into the workspace bucket; only the insert is suppressed.
samples.evidence: `const url = await upload(file);` (image-insert.ts:144) runs first and the `editor.isDisposed()` check is at 145-148. On the `/shared/:token` path `upload` is `shareTokenImageUploader(token)`, so the write lands via `POST /api/v1/shared/images?token=…`. Blast radius is bounded because that route re-checks the role server-side at request time (`assertCanWrite` → `link.role !== 'editor'` ⇒ 403, image-share-upload.controller.ts:135) and is throttled to 30/min, so a genuinely downgraded token is refused; what remains is an orphaned upload when disposal was for any other reason. Ordering the check before the upload (or re-checking both) would make the guard cover the side effect it is meant to stop.

samples.summary: `MUTATING_METHODS` is a deny-list, and this change promotes it from one gate (read-only mounts) to two (read-only *and* disposal) without adding any fail-closed mechanism — a future `EditorAPI` mutator not added to the list silently writes through both gates.
samples.evidence: `neuterMutations` iterates a hand-maintained name list (editor.ts:1046-1057) whose own comment says "Keep in sync when adding a mutating method", and read-only.ts:11-14 records that this exact list already failed open once by omitting `getStore`/`getDoc` (#989). The sibling gate inverted the direction for that reason (`DOC_STORE_READERS` is an allowlist of readers). Disposal now leans on the list for every `api` member that writes through the *raw* `docStore` rather than through the revocable handle — e.g. `stepSelectionFontSize` reaches `docStore.applyStyles` at editor.ts:1379 and `setDocStyles`/`updateStyleToMatch`/`resetNamedStyle`/`resetAllNamedStyles` reach `docStore.setDocStyles`/`updateStyleDefinition`/`resetStyle`/`resetAllStyles` at editor.ts:3559/3604/3607/3610 — so a missing name is a full write bypass, not a degraded read. I cross-checked the current interface and found no mutator missing today, hence minor: the finding is the absent fail-closed mechanism, not a live hole.
searchedFor: read the whole EditorAPI interface (editor.ts:53-438) and compared every member against MUTATING_METHODS
grep 'docStore\.' in packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts to find writes that bypass revocableStore
read restoreLocalCursor / validateCursorPosition / resetAfterDocumentReplace / updateCompositionStartPosition implementations to confirm they make no store writes
grep 'pageSetupGuardedStore|revocableStore|readStore' in editor.ts to confirm which handles are handed out
read api.paste (editor.ts:4001) to confirm it routes through the now-guarded TextEditor.pasteContent

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out. The mount effect (slides-view.tsx:238) lists `readOnlyMount` in its deps (line 1237, with a comment at 1226-1235 stating the point is to rebuild on an editor-to-viewer downgrade), so the body re-runs at revocation time. That body calls `ensureSlidesRoot(doc, ...)` at line 282 with no read-only check — the comment at 276-281 admits it is a viewer-write gap — and yorkie-slides-store.ts:246 opens `doc.update(...)` unconditionally, backfilling themes/masters/guides/meta.themeId/notes as the mounting principal. The sibling gate at slides-view.tsx:696 (`!readOnlyMount`) shows the read-only policy exists and that this path escapes it. No upstream guard neutralizes it: the server-side write gate (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:217, viewer never gets `rw`) is short-circuited to allow whenever YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE !== 'true' (lines 100-119), which docs/design/sharing.md:208 and docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:201 describe as the default, so client-side gating is the effective enforcement. The update body only emits ops on a not-yet-backfilled deck, which narrows exploitability but does not remove the unauthorized-write path — a nuance, not a named refutation ground. In lane: access control on a write performed by a session that lost write authority.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository. yorkie-auth.controller.ts:100-101 sets `enforce` only when YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true', and handleAuth:111-119 converts any deny decision into HTTP 200 `{allowed:true, reason:'shadow'}` when enforcement is off — the default. The per-document write decision it discards is real: checkAttribute:181 computes needWrite and hasAccess:217 returns `needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true` for anonymous share visitors, so this is the only server-side per-document write gate. With it in shadow mode, the write boundary for a revoked/downgraded share visitor is client-side only: readOnlyDocStore/revocableDocStore (read-only.ts:67-229) are Proxies running in the visitor's own page, and docs-view.tsx:404 attaches the live editor to `window.__docsEditor`. The source comments at read-only.ts:38-42 and shared-document.tsx:1099-1103 state the same conclusion, and self-hosting.md:185 documents the default as "log the decision, allow everything", while template-review.ts:80 and register-templates.ts:154-156 hard-require ENFORCE=true elsewhere — the codebase itself treats shadow mode as unprotected. Access control / weakened permission gate is in the Security lane; no guard elsewhere makes the shadow branch unreachable, and pre-existing/deployment-gated status does not refute it under the rubric.

verdict.reason: The described code is present verbatim: revocableDocStore's live branch forwards non-function members raw (read-only.ts:199), binds mutators to the raw target (read-only.ts:202), and forwards the real prototype (read-only.ts:214). YorkieDocStore.doc is a runtime own field (yorkie-doc-store.ts:576-577; `private` is TS-only) holding the Yorkie Document whose update() is the write path, and the public accessor does not hide it — getStore() returns pageSetupGuardedStore (editor.ts:3345) whose get trap also forwards non-functions raw (editor.ts:3319) through revocableStore. So `editor.getStore().doc`, or any bound mutator/prototype method captured before dispose, retains full CRDT write authority after `disposed = true`, and no later isRevoked() check is consulted on those captured references. This is in-lane authorization weakness, not a mere lifecycle bug: the repo itself frames disposal as the enforcement point for a writer->viewer role downgrade (editor.ts:4462-4480) and explicitly claims "even a handle captured before now goes dead" (editor.ts:4474-4475), while read-only.ts:89-96 hides data properties for exactly this reason and read-only.ts:38-42 / editor.ts:4535-4539 note the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow mode so this is the effective write boundary. No guard elsewhere closes it (neuterMutations at editor.ts:4482 only rewrites members of `api`). Exploitability depends on a pre-disposal capture, which I could not demonstrate from an in-repo holder, but the gate is genuinely bypassable and reads as complete — no refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: The entire downgrade/revocation boundary added here is client-side; with the default YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=false the Yorkie server still accepts writes from a viewer-role or revoked share token
finding.evidence: The comment at shared-document.tsx:1095 states it plainly: under the default `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=false` the docs read-only wrapper "is the write boundary the visitor actually meets". packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:185 confirms the default is shadow mode — "log the decision, allow everything" — and packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:101 gates enforcement on that env var being the string 'true'. Attack: hold an editor share token, keep the Yorkie attach (the auth token is injected at attach, shared-document.tsx:1009), let the owner downgrade the link to viewer or delete it; the new 60s poll only reconfigures this tab's React tree, so a modified client, a devtools console call, or a client that simply never re-polls keeps pushing changes and the server accepts them. Pre-existing posture rather than introduced here, and the repo tracks flipping the flag as a release precondition — but this PR builds its stated revocation guarantee on top of it, so the guarantee is advisory against a non-cooperating client.

verdict.reason: Evidence verified as described. yorkie-auth.controller.ts:100-101 gates enforcement on the exact string 'true', and lines 111-119 convert any computed deny into ALLOW when unset — so the only server-side role check for share visitors (hasAccess, line 217: `needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`) and the revoked-token deny (lines 213-220) are inert in the default configuration, which self-hosting.md:185 and backend/README.md:101-104 document as `false`/shadow. On the client, shared-document.tsx:1116-1129 only re-polls resolveShareLink to update `resolved`/`readOnly` in the React tree; the Yorkie auth token is injected at attach (line 1013) and no code path tears down or re-authorizes the live connection, so a modified or non-polling client keeps pushing writes with a downgraded or revoked token. The in-file comment at 1099-1103 concedes the wrapper is not the security boundary. I searched every use of the flag: the only hard preconditions (template-review.ts:77-83, template.service.ts:468-471, register-templates.ts:154-157) gate template publication only, not share-link creation/resolution, so `already-guarded` does not apply; the code is present as described so `not-present` does not apply; and a permission gate that is off the enforced path by default is core to the authorization lane, so `out-of-scope` does not apply.
